checked_claims.claim: Tuples directly contain themselves and recursion runs indefinitely
checked_claims.reason: Recursive traversal has no visited set, but ordinary tuple cannot directly self-reference; indirect cycles through mutable containers hit Python recursion limit rather than guaranteed native stack overflow.

material_errors: Recursive traversal has no visited set, but ordinary tuple cannot directly self-reference; indirect cycles through mutable containers hit Python recursion limit rather than guaranteed native stack overflow.
tasks.notes: Direct source review, no upstream execution.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: TagTuple.to_json recursively calls serializer.tag on each item; dispatch returns JSONTag.tag which calls the selected to_json (src/flask/json/tag.py:87-90,133-154,289-295). There is no cycle detection in this tagging traversal. A tuple can participate in an indirect cycle through a list/dict, causing repeated traversal and ordinarily RecursionError at Python recursion depth. Ordinary immutable tuples do not directly contain themselves; deep finite nesting is also depth-limited rather than an infinite cycle.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: TagMarkup.check tests whether __html__ is callable; to_json delegates to that method on the value and converts its result with str (src/flask/json/tag.py:181-185). The helper implementation belongs to the object class, not Flask. JSONTag.tag wraps the conversion under the tag key (src/flask/json/tag.py:87-90). The check does not prove the callable accepts zero arguments or cannot raise; errors from protocol invocation are not caught here.

checked_claims.claim: Read-only resource helper enforces global application-code immutability/security
checked_claims.reason: Helper restricts its modes but does not prevent other writes or enforce filesystem security; broad intent inferred.

material_errors: Helper restricts its modes but does not prevent other writes or enforce filesystem security; broad intent inferred.
tasks.notes: Direct source review, no upstream execution.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: open_resource permits only r, rt and rb and opens relative to root_path (src/flask/app.py:353-361). open_instance_resource explicitly allows writes relative to instance_path (src/flask/app.py:363-368). This API distinction separates reading packaged resources from mutable instance files. It is not a filesystem security boundary and cannot prevent writes through other APIs; stronger immutability claims are not established by this method.

checked_claims.reason: Conversion mechanism correct but sample compares independent random UUIDs, not same input.

material_errors: Conversion mechanism correct but sample compares independent random UUIDs, not same input.
tasks.notes: Direct source review, no upstream execution.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: TagUUID recognizes UUID instances, serializes value.hex under the " u" tag and reconstructs UUID(value) (src/flask/json/tag.py:191-202). TaggedJSONSerializer tags before dumping and recursively untags after loading (src/flask/json/tag.py:289-327), preserving UUID value/type through JSON. A valid roundtrip check uses u=uuid4(); s.loads(s.dumps(u)) == u, not a second uuid4() call.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: ScriptInfo starts with _loaded_app=None and load_app reuses a cached app (src/flask/cli.py:331-339). FlaskGroup looks up built-in/plugin commands before loading app-defined commands (src/flask/cli.py:609-634), permitting discovery when app loading fails. However, help command listing does attempt to load the app and catches failures while retaining built-ins (src/flask/cli.py:636-655). Lazy loading provides controlled timing and reuse; it does not mean every help request avoids imports.
